findings.message: the IR maps 'client_ip', 'dest_host', 'http_version', 'method', 'url', but no pattern captures them: the patterns capture only 'details', 'fd', 'level', 'message', 'pid', 'timestamp'. A mapping whose key is never extracted leaves its ECS field empty on every line. Add a named capture for each of these keys where its value sits in the line, or move the key to `unresolved`.

findings.message: the pattern matches 6 of 10 sample lines. It must match every one: a line it misses is dropped entirely, not partly parsed. The first it misses is 'NOTICE    Oct 27 16:11:26.677 [1]: Unauthorized connection from "172.21.66.211".'. Of the 4 patterns, the closest to it is '^%{WORD:level} +(?<timestamp>%{MONTH} +%{MONTHDAY} %{TIME}) \\[%{INT:pid}\\]: (?<action>Unauthorized connection) from "%{D'. the pattern matches up to %{IP:client_ip}, which fails on '172.21.66.211".'. The capture before it, %{DATA:client_name}, matched only '' and stopped at '172.21.66.21' - it is too narrow, and that is the one to widen It also misses lines of other shapes: 'CONNECT   Oct 27 16:11:23.436 [1]: Connect (file descriptor 6): 172.21.66.11'. If this line is a VARIANT of the others - an extra word, a field that is sometimes absent - make that part optional with (?:...)? rather than writing a second pattern. If it is a DIFFERENT KIND of message - different words, not one more of them - add a pattern for it to `alternatives`, reusing the same capture name for the same value.
'client_name' appears in 4/10 samples but is neither mapped nor listed as unresolved.

alternatives: ^%{WORD:level} +(?<timestamp>%{MONTH} +%{MONTHDAY} %{TIME}) \[%{INT:pid}\]: (?<action>Established connection) to host "%{DATA:dest_host}" using file descriptor %{INT:fd}\.$
^%{WORD:level} +(?<timestamp>%{MONTH} +%{MONTHDAY} %{TIME}) \[%{INT:pid}\]: (?<action>Established connection) to host "%{DATA:dest_host}" using file descriptor %{INT:fd}\.$

Those fields are declared in the mapping and absent from the output, so either the source key does not exist or the extraction is not reaching it.
the probe injected 'Invalid admin token' as event.reason, and it appears in no field of any parsed document. The parser dropped it.
